# ziiz — design system exploration

A sandbox for building my own design system, not a product. The goal is a system
that reads premium and distinct without looking like default shadcn — built by
porting Vercel's Geist token layer and then diverging deliberately.

**Current state (2026-08-15):** the token foundation is live end to end. The
Geist ramp (`--ds-*`), the shadcn slot aliases on top of it, the ramp exposed as
Tailwind utilities (`bg-gray-100`, `text-gray-900`, shadows), the 31 type roles,
and the 8 material utilities are all in `app/globals.css` and driving every
pixel. Inter ships locally with `cv05`/`ss03` on. The docs surface
(`/colors`, `/typography`, `/materials`) dogfoods all of it; `/` redirects to
`/colors`. The interaction signature is **adopted, in gray** (2026-08-15) —
offset ring + halo, both composed inline from ring utilities, applied per
component during migration.
Open work: migrating `components/ui` off alias vocabulary
(44 of 62 files still speak shadcn slots — stock, untouched) and one doc/code
mismatch on the input wash. See [Next step](#next-step).

---

## The core finding

Vercel's docs components **are** shadcn — same `cva` shape, same six variant
names, same `data-slot`, same Radix `Slot` for `asChild`. Card, badge, input,
kbd and spinner all match. Only the docs-specific pieces (code block, command
prompt, mermaid, video) are Vercel-authored.

So the premium read does not come from the components. It comes from four layers
sitting above them:

1. **Token vocabulary** — `--ds-gray-1000` not `--foreground`
2. **Typography as named roles** — `text-label-14` not `text-sm font-medium`
3. **Elevation as composed material** — hairline ring + tight shadow, radius pinned
4. **Interaction signature** — offset focus ring; hover steps the ramp, never `bg-primary/80`

That reframes the whole project: don't fork the components, fork these four.

# Color ramps

How the palette is generated, why it is shaped the way it is, and what to do
when you bring a new colour in.

Implementation: `lib/color-ramp.ts`. Live tool: `/playground`.

---

## 1. The mental model

A ramp is ten steps from a **floor** to a **ceiling**.

- **Floor** — `background-100`, the page. Dark's floor is its darkest colour;
  light's floor is its lightest. Either way it is where the eye rests.
- **Ceiling** — `gray-1000`, the strongest ink.
- **Anchors** — steps **700** (solid fill) and **800** (hover). These are the
  brand colours. Everything else is derived.

The axis the system actually works in is **contrast against the floor**, not
lightness. Contrast rises monotonically from step 100 to 1000 in both themes,
which is why one set of rules serves light and dark. Lightness only rises in
dark; in light it falls.

| steps   | role               | derived from    |
| ------- | ------------------ | --------------- |
| 100–200 | subtle background  | the floor       |
| 300–400 | subtle border      | the floor       |
| 500–600 | border             | floor → solid   |
| **700** | **solid fill**     | **anchor**      |
| **800** | **hover**          | **anchor**      |
| 900     | text               | hover → ceiling |
| 1000    | high-contrast text | the ceiling     |

I kept it faithful to the dump but organized it into labeled sections since it was really three sources:

1. **x.com primitives** — the `--color-*` / `--text-*` / `--font-*` Tailwind-style vars
2. **x.com semantic layer** — the `--x-*` tokens, dark then light
3. **x.ai** — the `--color-brand-*` 17-step ramps, then the named HSL palette + `--color-theme-*` aliases, light then dark

I also added a short header noting the scale quirks visible in the data, since that's what you're dissecting:

- x.com neutrals run **0 → 1100 inverted** (0 is near-white) and the semantic layer swaps `white-aN` ↔ `black-aN` alphas between themes — dark surfaces/borders are literally translucent white.
- x.com semantic tints use the **1100 steps in dark, 50 steps in light**.
- x.ai brand ramps use irregular steps (100–700 with 25s and 50s mixed in) with **400 as the mid pivot** — the dark ends (600–700) are near-black tints of the hue.
